expectations.text: Offers multiple-choice answer options where the question allows it
expectations.evidence: All four questions are open-ended free-text asks ('Cheapest paid plan price... a number or range', 'Gross margin %', 'Monthly churn %', 'Current or target CAC'). No lettered/numbered option sets or selectable bands are offered, even though several (margin band, churn band, pricing model, recurring vs flat structure) easily allow tap-friendly choices. The only scaffolding is illustrative parentheticals ('e.g. ~75-80%', 'or annual retention if that's what you track') and a single implicit escape hatch ('if you genuinely don't have churn or CAC numbers yet... tell me that too'), which is a fallba

expectations.text: Offers multiple-choice answer options where the question allows it
expectations.evidence: The answer commits to a single prescription ('30% recurring, capped at 12 months') and actively closes off alternatives rather than laying them out as selectable options: 'Skip tiers, loyalty bumps, or CPA-vs-revshare menus for launch.' The only trace of optionality is a conditional fallback buried in the last paragraph ('If your gross margin is under ~70%, drop to 20–25% instead'), which is a contingency note, not a presented choice set. The question — what commission rate/structure to put on the page — plainly admits discrete options (20/25/30%, lifetime vs capped, revshare vs CPA vs hybrid)
